main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise. A symmetrical 1,598m country oval featuring a downhill run along the backstretch from the 1400m mark to the 800m turn, followed by a slight uphill rise into the 380m home straight. The downhill run encourages early speed, but the uphill finish acts as a stamina filter, giving patient stalkers ('P') and closers ('C') a fair opportunity.
main_turf.post_bias: In 1100m and 1200m sprint starts, inside-to-middle barriers (stalls 1-5) are preferred to secure a ground-saving trip before entering the sweeping home bend. Over 1400m and 1800m route distances, starting chute run-ups make the draw relatively fair.

handicapping_angles.downhill_backstretch_uphill_straight_fil: The downhill run from the 1400m to 800m turn causes overly aggressive front-runners ('E') to burn early fuel. Look for patient pressers ('P') who can conserve energy before unleashing down the uphill 380m home stretch.
handicapping_angles.provincial_and_sydney_shipper_advantage: Trainers shipping in from Sydney midweek or Provincial bases (Warwick Farm, Hawkesbury, Kembla Grange, Goulburn) carry a distinct speed and class advantage over local Central West country runners.
handicapping_angles.bathurst_cup_showcase_class_spike: During the autumn Bathurst Cup Showcase meeting, fields feature high-grade regional and provincial opposition. Prioritize horses with proven metro/provincial speed figures over local country lines.
handicapping_angles.nsw_country_benchmark_weight_penalty: In NSW Country Benchmark handicaps (BM58-BM74), top weights carrying 60kg+ face a compounding penalty on the uphill home stretch (1kg = ~1 length). Grant a boost to fit, light-weighted runners receiving relief.
